subject: Ashby Labs service impact — throughput spike, error surge, and remediation
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@ashby.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alison Meyer <ali.meyer@ashby.ai>
Date: Sat, 05 Dec 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Ashby — surge: high 5xx, degraded throughput during batch window

Hi Priyom,

We ran our nightly ingest batch this morning (00:00–03:00 PST) and saw a sustained throughput drop and elevated 5xx rates that caused roughly 28% of our records to fail and large backpressure across downstream queues. Latency also jumped — P95 doubled compared to baseline. This is materially impacting our downstream ETL and our SLAs to customers.

I attached logs (ashby_logs_20261205.zip) and a short extract of failed request IDs. Can you please escalate: we need a remediation plan, an estimate of customer-facing impact, and confirmation of any contractual credits/remedies under our MSA (Section 5.2). We are preparing an exec forum if needed.

Thanks,
Daniel
Director of Platform Engineering
Ashby Labs

---

Thanks for the logs and the heads-up. I've looped in Ben (AE), Mina (CS lead) and Laura (legal). We take this seriously and want to get a clear remediation and commercial path quickly.

- Ben and I will work through contractual remedies and an initial credit envelope we can propose.

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 05 Dec 2026 12:45:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Ashby — surge: high 5xx, degraded throughput during batch window

On Sat, Dec 5, 2026 at 10:02 AM Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Daniel —
> Thanks for the logs and the heads-up. I've looped in Ben...

Team — quick summary from an infra perspective after a first pass on the logs Daniel sent:
- Root cause: an autoscaler regression combined with a KV-cache invalidation bug. Under the specific traffic spike during Ashby's batch window, we hit a pathological scheduling path that delayed container warmup and dropped requests (5xx).
- Impact window (observed): 2026-12-05T00:47:00Z through 2026-12-05T03:22:00Z (UTC).
- Quantified: ~28% of batch requests returned 5xx; median latency increased from ~120ms to ~420ms for affected workers.
- Mitigation applied: disabled the aggressive autoscaler rule and patched the cache check; we validated recovery at 03:40 UTC.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Full RCA write-up (ETA: 48 hours).
2) A backfill plan for any failed batch records (we can provide a re-run window or a one-time assisted backfill).
3) Commercial calculation (credit) tied to the exact outage window and contract SLA formula.

I'll produce an ops summary and the raw trace links in the shared drive.

-Vivek
VP, Engineering (Serving Runtime)
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@ashby.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 06 Dec 2026 09:08:00 -08:00
Subject: Proposed commercial remedy and next steps (Ashby)

Daniel —

Appreciate the call-outs and logs. Based on Vivek's initial impact window and your note on downstream SLA exposure, we propose the following commercial remediation as a starting point for negotiation:

Proposal (initial):
- Service credit equal to 15% of Ashby's December monthly invoice, applied as account credit, reflecting the service degradation during the 2 hour 35 minute impact window.
- One-time assisted re-run of failed batch processing at no charge (engineering time + compute covered by Redwood).
- Priority monitoring & a post-incident review with your engineering leads, including a follow-up that maps mitigations to our autoscaling configs.

Rationale: per Section 5.2 of the MSA the credit formula uses the proportional downtime / impact. Given the partial degradation and the fact that services recovered inside the batch window after mitigations, 15% is our starting industry-aligned offer.

We can escalate to an exec review and expand the credit if Ashby demonstrates broader contractual breach (e.g., repeated monthly misses). Laura, please flag any legal considerations if we need to convert this to a formal amendment or sign a one-off settlement.

If this is acceptable as a starting point, we can prepare the credit worksheet and a DocuSign amendment for signature.

-Ben
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Proposed commercial remedy and next steps (Ashby)

Ben/Priyom —

Thank you for the quick analysis and the concrete offer. A few clarifying points from Ashby:
- We appreciate the assisted re-run, but we need a guarantee window for completion (earliest completion date).
- Regarding the credit, Ashby prefers a cash rebate or invoice offset rather than credits applied to future usage; procurement will confirm which is permissible.
- We would like senior exec alignment prior to signing a settlement (Ashby CTO will join an exec call).

Can Redwood provide a final credit amount (USD) and a draft amendment/settlement doc for legal to review before an exec call? The DocuSign link would be helpful.

Regards,
Alison Meyer
VP, Revenue Operations
Ashby Labs

Date: Tue, 09 Dec 2026 16:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Settlement terms and exec meeting — Ashby Labs

Alison —

Thanks for the clarity. Redwood can confirm the following:

Final settlement (subject to signature):
- One-time invoice offset of $24,500 (representing 15% of the billed December service fee under Deal ASH-2026-1427).
- Commitment to complete the assisted backfill within 5 business days after countersignature; Redwood engineering will provide a runbook and an ETA during the post-incident plan meeting.
- A 60-day operational follow-up including a joint RCA and mitigation mapping.

I attach a draft settlement amendment (DocuSign prepared) and the credit calculation workbook; please review and provide any redlines. Once Ashby's legal countersigns we can schedule the exec alignment call (we recommend a 30-minute slot, Redwood VP and VP Eng to join).

If procurement needs cash rebate instead of invoice offset, please confirm and we will route through finance — that will delay payment timing but is feasible.

-Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
